en.sig.camera.d: While you play a game or do the check-in, the camera notices smiles, eyebrow and mouth movement, blinks, whether you look toward the screen, and how much your head and face move. This device turns them into numbers, and only the numbers are sent. It also notices when an expression stays lower, more tense or brighter for a while than earlier in the same activity. In a check-in, Kaiku may then ask one gentle question; it never says what it noticed, and it is not a statement about how you feel. No pictures are kept or sent, and Kaiku does not label emotions. You see the numbers in History. Your care team sees them beside your record, and the numbers decide nothing.

en.sig.see.t: Let Kaiku see through the glasses during walks
en.sig.look.d: Let the Gemma model look at a few pictures from the camera during a check-in. The pictures are sent to Google's servers, where that model runs, and are not saved by Kaiku; only what the model notes is kept. It needs Camera during activities to be on. Up to three small pictures of one check-in go from this device to the Kaiku service once, and from there to Kaiku's model (Gemma, run for Kaiku through Google's Gemini API), which answers with a few fixed words: whether a face is in view, whether it looks resting, smiling, lowered or tense, where you are looking, how you are sitting, and the light. Those words are kept beside your record; your care team sees them, and they decide nothing. It is a description of a picture, not a statement about how you feel. If the send fails, the pictures are dropped, not sent again.

fi.sig.camera.d: While you play a game or do the check-in, the camera notices smiles, eyebrow and mouth movement, blinks, whether you look toward the screen, and how much your head and face move. This device turns them into numbers, and only the numbers are sent. It also notices when an expression stays lower, more tense or brighter for a while than earlier in the same activity. In a check-in, Kaiku may then ask one gentle question; it never says what it noticed, and it is not a statement about how you feel. No pictures are kept or sent, and Kaiku does not label emotions. You see the numbers in History. Your care team sees them beside your record, and the numbers decide nothing.

fi.sig.look.d: Let the Gemma model look at a few pictures from the camera during a check-in. The pictures are sent to Google's servers, where that model runs, and are not saved by Kaiku; only what the model notes is kept. It needs Camera during activities to be on. Up to three small pictures of one check-in go from this device to the Kaiku service once, and from there to Kaiku's model (Gemma, run for Kaiku through Google's Gemini API), which answers with a few fixed words: whether a face is in view, whether it looks resting, smiling, lowered or tense, where you are looking, how you are sitting, and the light. Those words are kept beside your record; your care team sees them, and they decide nothing. It is a description of a picture, not a statement about how you feel. If the send fails, the pictures are dropped, not sent again.
